verdicts.evidence: lines 456-489: every Copy button gets a click handler that copies the command; 539-560: each tab has click and key handlers that switch panels; 261-262: native details/summary toggles the contents list on narrow screens.
Static documentation page; no records, counts, metrics or charts drawn from a data source. The requirements table (293-302) is fixed text from the brief.
All steps are on one page (lines 307-395); the list step and the restore step that uses its snapshot id are both visible by scrolling, with no separate screens.
No inputs, forms or free text anywhere in the file.

lines 507-514, 561: the only preselected value is the operating system tab, chosen from the browser platform with macOS as fallback; it only changes which command is shown and loses nothing. No dialogs or default buttons.
lines 456-489: the frequent task, copying a command, is one click on the Copy button beside each command, on the same page with no dialog.

lines 384-387: 'Try a restore now' callout is advice not in the notes; 335 'open a new terminal window', 395 'Cron is not available on Windows', 357-358 PowerShell commands and 391 'crontab -e' are additions not supplied by the brief.
lines 155-163, 171-177: Copy buttons and tabs all use plain secondary styles; no button anywhere uses a filled primary style, so no region has more than one primary.
No control on the page deletes, overwrites or performs an irreversible action; the only controls are Copy, tabs and the contents toggle.
No disabled attribute or disabled styling anywhere in the markup or script.
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards in the file.
lines 250-418: visible text covers only harbour, its commands and the reader's setup task; no mention of framework, the request, mock data or unfinished features.

lines 366-369: passphrase warning sits at the passphrase choice and tells the reader to save it; 384-387: restore note sits at the restore command; 395: cron note sits at the schedule step. Each has a nameable action beside it.
line 279: 'This page takes you from nothing installed to a backup that runs every night.' narrates the page itself, the 'This page lets you' pattern the rule excludes.
lines 281-288: the 'What you will do' box restates the lede sentence at 279 and the contents list at 263-273 (install, create repository, back up, list, restore, schedule) in other words.
lines 278-418: no greetings, slogans, superlatives or exclamation marks; headings are 'Getting started', 'Install harbour', 'Create a repository' and claims name commands, versions and sizes.

line 461: button label is the verb 'Copy', placed inside the command box it acts on, with aria-label 'Copy command: ...' (462); it changes to 'Copied' (467). Contents toggle reads 'Show' / 'Hide' (228-229).
lines 338, 378: 'repository' and 'snapshot' are defined in plain words; code terms shown (HARBOUR_S3_KEY, --overwrite) are things the reader must type, not internal labels.

lines 470-478: when copying fails the command text is selected, the button reads 'Selected' and the message says 'Could not copy automatically. The command is selected, press Ctrl or Command and C.' No codes or exception text.
line 478: 'Could not copy automatically. The command is selected, press Ctrl or Command and C.' No blame words, exclamation marks or capitals. Warning at 367-368 states the fact plainly.
No list, table, feed or search that can have zero items; all content is fixed markup.
No filters, search or loaded data, so no view can be empty.
Fully static page; the script (424-604) makes no fetch or other server request.
No action waits on a server; clipboard write and tab switching resolve at once (433-438, 519-527).
No asynchronous data, loading state or empty state.
Only fixed text is displayed; nothing varies in length or count at run time. Long commands scroll inside their box (148-152).
No editable content or explicit save.
No form fields on the page.
No form fields on the page.
No form or validation on the page.
No form that can reject input.
No form that can be rejected.
No form that can reject input.
No form or submit button on the page.
No form with a server effect.
lines 464-469: Copy changes its label to 'Copied' and turns green as soon as the clipboard promise resolves; 519-525: a tab click switches the selected state and panel synchronously.
lines 467-469: success shows 'Copied' on the button; 472-478: failure selects the command and shows 'Selected'; 522-524: the chosen tab is marked and its panel shown.
line 467: the only success message is 'Copied' on the button; the clipboard change is not otherwise visible on screen, so the message reports something the user could not see.

lines 479-486: the same 2 second timer runs after the failure branch, resetting 'Selected' to 'Copy' and clearing the 'Could not copy automatically... press Ctrl or Command and C' text, so the error and its instruction auto-dismiss.
No action on the page removes, archives, moves or changes anything.
No irreversible action is performed by the page; destructive commands are only shown as text.
No confirmation dialogs; no confirm() call or dialog element in the file.
No optimistic updates and no server requests.
No modal dialog in markup or script.
No modal dialog in markup or script.

lines 277-307: main opens with the h1, one lede paragraph, a short summary box and requirements, then the install step; the contents list is a narrow side column (83) or a collapsed bar on phones (569). Steps carry the largest headings.
lines 278-279: the page opens with 'Getting started' and one sentence saying what harbour is; no hero, greeting or full-height panel, and the opening is sized to its content (106-107).
No stat cards, summary numbers or charts.
No filtering, search or sorting of any view.

lines 458-459: Copy controls are native buttons; 547-557: tabs use roving tabindex with arrow, Home and End keys; 261-262: native details; 492-503: overflowing command blocks get tabindex 0 so they can be scrolled by keyboard.

lines 162, 467: green done state also changes text to 'Copied'; 177: selected tab has an underline bar as well as colour; 102: current contents link gets a side bar and bold weight; 154: placeholders are italic as well as coloured.
line 422: an aria-live polite region exists in the page on load; 469 and 478 fill it with 'Copied to clipboard' or the could-not-copy message.
lines 519-525: each tab's aria-selected is set true or false on every selection and its panel hidden accordingly; 261: the contents list uses a native details element.

lines 215-236: under 860px the layout becomes one column with 16px gutters, the contents list becomes a collapsible bar, commands scroll inside their box (150) with Copy still visible (155-156), the tab list wraps (169) and the table sits in a scroll wrapper (193).
lines 588-598: the scroll handler sets aria-current on the contents link for the section in view; 102: that link gets accent colour, a left bar and weight 600, so the cue is more than colour.

lines 543-546, 555-556: choosing an operating system tab only changes DOM state; nothing writes it to the URL or reads it back, and 561 re-runs detection on load, so a reload or shared link returns to the detected system rather than the chosen tab.
Single page with one view; section links at 264-272 are native in-page anchors and the script adds no history handling.
lines 412-416: the page ends with links to /docs/excludes, /docs/retention and /docs/check; 263-273 link to every section. The breadcrumb at 254 is plain text, not a link.
No dialog or overlay in the file.

lines 307-389: Steps 1 to 6 are all on one page and each depends on the one before (install, create repository, back up, list, restore by id, schedule); it starts on a working step with no welcome screen.

lines 99, 231: at phone width the contents links are 0.93rem text at line-height 1.35 with 9px top and bottom padding, about 38px tall, under 44px. Copy buttons (156) and tabs (174) do have min-height 44px.

line 89: the only sticky element is the contents list in its own 220px grid column (83), so it does not overlay the content; 222: it becomes position static under 860px. The skip link is off screen until focused (61-65).

lines 278-279: heading 'Getting started' and the line under it: 'harbour makes encrypted, de-duplicated backups of your folders to a local disk or to any S3-compatible storage.' A reader can say what it is and that it is for backing up their own folders.
Documentation article with no main call to action; the reader works through the steps in order.
No img, svg, video or generated graphics in the file.
No testimonials, customer names, usage figures, ratings or prices on the page.
No pricing section.
No images or video.
No announcement or promotional strip; the top bar (250-256) holds only the name, version and breadcrumb.
lines 456-489: every .cmd block gets a 'Copy' button with an aria-label naming the command; it copies the block text and changes to 'Copied' (467), with a live announcement (469).

lines 16, 35: one accent hue (blue-teal) used for links (56), the current contents item (102), step labels (114), the selected tab (177) and placeholders (154). Amber (21-23) and green (24) are status colours only.
